title: Does Giving the Judge a Checklist Beat Giving It a Debate?

original_idea.body:
# Does Giving the Judge a Checklist Beat Giving It a Debate?

**Problem:** Whether cheap structured prompting matches debate's accuracy gains is unknown.

**Direction:** On QuALITY/reasoning judging, compare three conditions at matched judge cost: plain direct-QA judging, single-round debate, and a checklist-guided judge. Report accuracy and token cost per condition across open judges.

**Why it matters:** If a cheap checklist captures most of debate's benefit, oversight becomes far more accessible.

**Relevant context:** Kenton et al. (2024); Kirchner et al. (2024); arXiv:2504.03731.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (cheaper oversight scaffold) but a checklist-vs-debate comparison is incremental, with a gap to catastrophic-risk reduction.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Three prompt-only judging conditions on existing tasks; accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped 3-condition cost-matched comparison with clear metrics.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Cheap-oversight-scaffold comparison on public models; external-friendly.

novelty.reasoning: Structured-verification prompting and debate exist; the head-to-head cost-matched comparison may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Components exist; the specific comparison plausibly open.
